provisions.text: Denied-party and sanctions screening is never bypassed, suppressed, allow-listed, or served from a cache older than 24 hours on any payment, onboarding, or beneficiary path. (Sanctions floor — 31 CFR Ch. V; IEEPA, 50 U.S.C. §1701. Liability is strict: there is no risk appetite to spend.)

No change may suppress, delay, or silently degrade suspicious-activity detection or filing, and no change may disclose the existence of a SAR to its subject. (BSA floor — 31 U.S.C. §5318(g); 31 CFR §1020.320. Tipping off is a criminal offence.)
No account is opened, funded, or raised in limit before the Customer Identification Program completes. (BSA floor — 31 CFR §1020.220.)

Sensitive authentication data — full track data, card verification codes, PINs and PIN blocks — is never retained after authorization, and the PAN is never written unmasked to a log. (Card-network floor — PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 3.3.1 and 3.4.1.)
EU/EEA personal data does not leave the region without an Article 45 adequacy decision or an Article 46 safeguard in force for that destination. (GDPR floor — Reg. (EU) 2016/679 Arts. 44-49.)
No prohibited-basis attribute, and no proxy for one, enters a credit underwriting, pricing, or line-assignment model. (Fair-lending floor — ECOA, 15 U.S.C. §1691; Reg. B, 12 CFR §1002.6(b)(9).)

No system performs social scoring, deploys subliminal or purposefully manipulative techniques, infers emotion in the workplace, or builds facial-recognition databases by untargeted scraping. (EU AI Act floor — Reg. (EU) 2024/1689 Art. 5, applicable since 2 February 2025.)
No change removes segregation of duties or disables the audit trail on a system inside the financial-reporting boundary. (SOX floor — 15 U.S.C. §7262; SEC Rule 13a-15.)
Consumer liability caps and error-resolution clocks for electronic fund transfers are not configurable downward or extendable by product decision. (Reg. E floor — 12 CFR §§1005.6, 1005.11.)

No adverse credit action rests on a model output that cannot produce specific principal reasons, and no change removes the human-reviewable path to contest one. (ECOA floor — 12 CFR §1002.9; CFPB Circulars 2022-03 and 2023-03: model complexity is not a defence.)

No autonomous agent moves customer funds, changes a credit limit, or closes an account without a bounded mandate and a human-operable stop, and no change removes or degrades that stop. (Oversight floor — Anthropic, Claude's Constitution (January 2026, CC0), which places not undermining appropriate human oversight above helpfulness; cf. EU AI Act Art. 14, SR 11-7 §V.)

Customer information is encrypted in transit and at rest; a change that weakens or removes encryption on a customer-data path requires the CISO's written finding of an effective alternative control. (GLBA Safeguards Rule — 16 CFR §314.4(c)(3), which contemplates exactly this finding.)

Multi-factor authentication protects every individual's access to every information system; any exception requires a written, CISO-approved compensating control reviewed at least annually. (23 NYCRR §500.12 — universal MFA in force since 1 November 2025; §500.12(a) permits CISO-approved compensating controls.)

No change disables or delays the telemetry that feeds regulatory incident reporting. (23 NYCRR §500.17(a), 72 hours; DORA Art. 19 with RTS (EU) 2025/301 — initial report 4 hours from classification, intermediate 72 hours, final one month.)

No ICT third party enters a critical-or-important function path without a register-of-information entry, a documented exit strategy, and disclosure of subcontracting. (DORA Art. 28(3), Reg. (EU) 2022/2554; register format per ITS (EU) 2024/2956.)
A change to a critical-or-important function is resilience tested before release; designated functions additionally carry threat-led penetration testing every three years. (DORA Arts. 24-26.)
No credential, key, or token appears in source, configuration, or CI logs; secrets live in the vault. (GLBA Safeguards 16 CFR §314.4(c); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 8.6.2.)

Every script on a payment page is authorized, inventoried, and integrity-checked, and a tamper-detection mechanism watches the page. (PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 6.4.3 and 11.6.1 — mandatory since 31 March 2025.)
No production change to a cardholder or ledger system without documented approval, a tested rollback, and separation between author and approver. (PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 6.5.1; SOC 2 CC8.1.)

Deploys are blocked on a greater-than-10% p95 latency regression, or any availability regression, on the payment-authorization path. (Operational provision; FFIEC Business Continuity Management Handbook.)

Personal data is collected for a stated purpose and deleted on schedule; no new personal-data field is retained without a recorded retention decision. (GDPR Arts. 5(1)(c) and 5(1)(e); CCPA/CPRA, Cal. Civ. Code §1798.100(c).)
No third-party code enters a cardholder-data or personal-data path without a completed vendor security review. (Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships, 88 FR 37920 (2023); DORA Art. 28.)

No production deploy during a designated market-close or peak-period change freeze except under the emergency protocol. (Operational provision; FFIEC Architecture, Infrastructure and Operations Handbook.)

No model reaches a credit, fraud, or AML decision in production before independent validation covering conceptual soundness, outcomes analysis, and ongoing monitoring. (SR 11-7 / OCC Bulletin 2011-12, Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management.)

Every model in a decision path carries an inventory entry and current documentation: purpose, training data, known limits, and a named owner. (SR 11-7 §VII model inventory; NIST AI RMF 1.0, GOVERN-1.)

A customer interacting with an AI system is told so, and synthetic content the firm generates is machine-markable. (EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency obligations, applicable from 2 August 2026; reinforced by CFPB UDAAP.)

Creditworthiness and credit-scoring systems are Annex III high-risk: risk management, data governance, logging, human oversight, and accuracy obligations must be in place before the applicable date. (EU AI Act Arts. 9-15 and Annex III(5)(b). The AI Omnibus, in force 27 July 2026, moved standalone Annex III obligations to 2 December 2027 and Annex I to 2 August 2028; the Art. 5 prohibitions and Art. 50 transparency duties were NOT deferred.)

A decisioning model is tested for disparate impact across protected classes before deployment and monitored afterwards. (NIST AI RMF 1.0, MEASURE-2.11; Reg. B effects test, 12 CFR §1002.6(a); CFPB Circular 2022-03.)

An AI-facing surface does not deceive a customer, impersonate a human, manufacture confidence it does not have, or steer a customer against their own interest. (Anthropic, Claude's Constitution (January 2026, CC0), honesty and non-manipulation; enforceable against the firm through UDAAP, 12 U.S.C. §5531.)

Every agent-authored change carries a provenance attestation — agent identity, model version, and a link to the originating human requirement — and every agent action in production runs under an explicit value and rate bound. (Firm oversight provision; SR 11-7 §V on model use controls; NIST AI RMF 1.0, MANAGE-4.)

No customer personal data enters model training, or a third party model provider's retention window, without a lawful basis and a contractual carve-out. (GLBA §502, 15 U.S.C. §6802; GDPR Art. 6; provider relationship governed by DORA Art. 28.)
No dark pattern, no material omission, and no fee or term a reasonable consumer would not expect from the disclosure given. (Dodd-Frank §§1031 and 1036, 12 U.S.C. §§5531 and 5536.)

Data furnished to consumer reporting agencies is accurate, disputes are investigated within the statutory window, and adverse action notices name both the reasons and the agency. (FCRA, 15 U.S.C. §§1681m and 1681s-2; Reg. V, 12 CFR Part 1022.)
Cost-of-credit disclosures are accurate, timely, and in the required form before the consumer becomes bound. (TILA, 15 U.S.C. §1601; Reg. Z, 12 CFR Part 1026.)

Opt-out of sale or sharing, and limits on sensitive personal information, are honoured on every surface including newly built ones. (CCPA/CPRA, Cal. Civ. Code §1798.100 et seq., and analogous state statutes.)

Consumer-permissioned data access is built to a documented interface with revocable authorization, whatever shape the rule finally takes. (Dodd-Frank §1033; 12 CFR Part 1033. The October 2024 final rule was enjoined by the Eastern District of Kentucky in October 2025 and is under CFPB reconsideration, so this is a READINESS provision with no live compliance date — the architecture, not the deadline, is what binds here.)
Consumer complaints are logged, routed, and closed within the stated window, and no change removes a complaint path without an equivalent replacement. (CFPB supervisory expectations; UDAAP.)

standing_declaration.note: No party in this deployment holds contest standing adverse to grants: contest may be invoked by the requesting party only, and the companion chapter's standing extension is not adopted. Recorded per Axiom A9 so that the one-sidedness of the realised base is a disclosed fact of every audit export.
